EXPLANATION: The spectrum looks like an aromatic molecule that has both aliphatic and aromatic C-H groups, a phenolic O–H, and a secondary amine:  
• 3057 cm⁻¹ (aromatic C–H stretch) and 2921 cm⁻¹ (aliphatic C–H stretch) show both ring and side-chain hydrogens, matching an ethyl-substituted phenol.  
• The very strong 1004 cm⁻¹ ring-breathing band is characteristic of a mono- or para-disubstituted benzene; CCNc1ccc(O)cc1 has that pattern.  
• 1380 and 1449 cm⁻¹ correspond to CH₃ symmetric / asymmetric deformations of the ethyl group.  
• 1247 cm⁻¹ fits the aromatic C–O stretch of a phenol.  
• 1613 cm⁻¹ can be assigned to N–H bending of a secondary amine (rule GFQ-002) overlapping the aromatic C=C stretch.  
• Out-of-plane C–H modes of a singly substituted ring commonly appear near 720–760 cm⁻¹, matching the observed 721 and 746 cm⁻¹.  
Taken together, the only candidate that simultaneously provides an aromatic ring, a phenolic O–H, an ethyl group (giving CH₃ bands) and an NH group is candidate 1 (CCNc1ccc(O)cc1).
